subject: High latency & 500s in production — suspect KV cache instability
messages:
From: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@edgescale.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@edgescale.com
Date: Mon, 22 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: High latency & 500s on production - suspect KV cache instability

Hi Jordan / Marissa,

We're seeing a sustained spike in gen latency and ~3-5% 500s on our production endpoints starting ~08:45 PDT. The errors correlate with large batched requests from our ingestion workers. P99 latency for text-generation has jumped from ~270ms to ~1.8s and request throughput dropped by ~25%.

We've attached a perf dump and a small KV snapshot. Initial look shows a lot of cache evictions and prefix miss churn in the logs. Can you escalate? This is impacting feature flag rollout and a few paying customers are reporting timeouts.

Symptoms observed:
- P99 spike: 270ms -> 1.8s (08:45–09:05)
- 500s ~3-5% for gen endpoints (mostly during burst windows)
- KV eviction peaks aligned with the spikes

We need a triage plan and a mitigation path — will accept short maintenance window if it helps.

Thanks,
Alex Rivera
CTO, EdgeScale

Attachments: perf_dump-edgescale-20270322.tar.gz; kv_snapshot-20270322.json

Alex — thanks for the heads up and the artifacts. I'm escalating this to infra and CS immediately. Quick plan:

2) CS (Monica/Marissa) to coordinate maintenance window and customer comms.
3) Execs (Evelyn) for any credit/SLA decisions if impact persists.

Alex — can you confirm the maintenance window you can accept today (we can do a 30m window starting ~10:30 PDT)? Also, please share any recent config changes on your side (batch sizing, prefix map changes).

Markus / Monica / Marissa / Evelyn — looping you in. Markus, attaching the perf dump Alex sent. Priority: high (customer impact + potential regression after last cache config rollout).

Thanks,
Jordan

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@edgescale.com>
Cc: monica_patel@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 22 Mar 2027 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: High latency & 500s on production - suspect KV cache instability

I've pulled the traces from the perf dump. Initial findings (high level):

- Root cause hypothesis: hot-prefix thrash causing head-of-line blocking when batches hit the same KV slices. The workload has a bimodal key distribution and our recent prefix-aggregation change reduced the effective sharding which increased local eviction pressure.
- Evidence: repeated cache miss / refill cycles for identical prefixes, large backpressure on batch lanes (seen as queueing and delayed kernel dispatch), and sharp increases in evictions per-second in the KV layer.
- Impact: increased per-token service latency due to synchronous KV refill on the hot path; some requests time out and return 500s.

Immediate mitigation (recommended, low-risk):
1) Roll back the recent prefix-aggregation change (KVConfig_v2 -> restore previous shard selectors) — avoids collisions. This is a config flip; low-risk and reversible.
2) Reduce max_batch_size from 64 -> 32 for 30 minutes to reduce hol blocking while we stabilize cache behavior.
3) Enable temporary soft-sticky routing for top 5% of keys (warm cache placement) and pre-warm top prefixes via a small async walker.
4) Increase KV cache capacity on the affected pool by +20% (if capacity available) or move critical shards to an isolated pool.

I'll prepare KVConfig_v3.patch with the rollback + sharding tweak and a short runbook for safe rollback. ETA to stage the config change: ~20–30m. ETA to complete change and observe: 45–60m.

Attaching: KVConfig_v3.patch, kv_snapshot-20270322.json (extracted hot-prefix list), perf_dump-edgescale-20270322.tar.gz

-Markus
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference

If you agree, we will:
- Schedule change for 10:30 PDT

- If latency metrics do not improve by 10:50, we will revert and open a follow-up incident timeline

For impact context: the outage window affected two customers with real-time pipelines (payment enrichment) — they saw ~10% request loss during the spike. We can provide customer ids if that helps prioritization. Please confirm when the patch is applied and when you see p99 back to baseline.

Regards,
Alex
